lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.unitTitle: PF2 — Buying Goods and Services: Major Purchase Analysis Under Constraint
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: total cost of ownership over a holding period

focus: total cost of ownership over a holding period
objective: Build the total cost of owning a fictional used vehicle across a five-year holding period, including resale, and convert it into a cost per year and a cost per mile.
scenario: Ines Kowalczyk-Amadi is a fictional buyer in a simulated town. The vehicle, its running costs, and its resale value below are invented figures and describe no real car or dealer.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional vehicle cost figures in these directions

tasks.directions: The fictional vehicle costs $14,800 to buy. Ines expects to drive 11,000 miles a year for 5 years, a total of 55,000 miles. It averages 25 miles per gallon and fuel costs $3.45 a gallon throughout.

prompts.text: How many gallons of fuel does Ines use in one year, driving 11,000 miles at 25 miles per gallon?
What does a year of fuel cost at $3.45 a gallon?
What does fuel cost across the whole 5 years?

tasks.directions: The other running costs are insurance at $1,340 a year, maintenance at $620 a year, and registration at $148 a year, all held flat across the 5 years.

prompts.text: What does insurance cost across the 5 years?
What do maintenance and registration cost together across the 5 years?
What is the total running cost across the 5 years, before the purchase price or resale are counted?

tasks.directions: At the end of the 5 years Ines expects to sell the vehicle for $5,900. Work these without help.

prompts.text: What is the total cost of owning the vehicle for 5 years, counting the purchase price and the running costs and subtracting the resale?
What does the vehicle cost per year across the holding period?
What does the vehicle cost per mile across the 55,000 miles?
Ignoring the purchase price itself, which single running cost is the largest across the 5 years?

tasks.directions: Answer each in a few sentences.

prompts.text: The vehicle’s price is $14,800 and owning it for five years costs $27,030.00. Explain where the extra cost comes from, and say which of the figures in the calculation you would least trust to hold for five years.

Ines is offered a similar vehicle at $12,900 that averages 19 miles per gallon. Say which figure in your calculation that change moves, and roughly how much of the $1,900 price saving it would consume.

remediation: If the five-year total comes out at $32,930.00, the resale value is being added instead of subtracted. The $5,900 is money coming back to Ines at the end, so it reduces what the five years cost. Lay the calculation out as three lines — money out for the purchase, money out for running costs, money back at the end — and check the sign on each line before totalling.
extension: Recompute the cost per mile if Ines drives 6,000 miles a year instead of 11,000, and say why the cost per mile rises even though the total cost falls.
